headline: Frenzy, in balance: AI is keeping pace with its price, for now

lines.label: Frontier AI capability
lines.note: METR 50% task length, Horizon v1.1; last measured 2026-04-07

lines.label: Capability, estimated
lines.note: fit on 18 models with both scores, R² 0.86; range ±1 SD (1.9×)

indicators.note: ARC-AGI-3: <1% at launch (Mar 25 2026) to 62.7% (GPT-6 Astra, Sep 3 2026, standard harness).
Epoch: ~47%/quarter (~13x/yr) across 5 benchmarks since 2023; 75x/yr at SOTA. Methodologies differ from the a16z estimate.
Oct 2025 to Oct 2026: OpenAI ~10, Anthropic ~13 frontier-tier releases; Google, xAI ~6.

OpenAI ~$50B (FT, end-Sep 2026) + Anthropic ~$65B (Bloomberg, end-Jul 2026) = ~$115B vs. ~$18B a year earlier (~$13B + ~$5B, recalled). Caveat: OpenAI figures were revised down ~$20B on definitions; Anthropic books some cloud-partner sales gross.
Sep 7-20 2026 period, released Oct 8. 27.7% expect use within 6 months. Not yet confirmed on census.gov.
Azure +43%, Google Cloud +82%, AWS +36.7% (Q2 2026). Calendar Q3 results due late October.
Q2 FY27 data center $89.0B, +18% QoQ. Q3 guide $108B total ex-China; reports late November.
Google model APIs 16B to 22B tokens/min, Q1 to Q2 2026, annualised. OpenRouter suggests far faster (~20x) but sources conflict; conservative figure used.
Q2 2026 YoY (+1.4% q/q annualised). Above the 2010s ~1.2% average; no clear AI-driven break yet.
Rough: Big-4 2026 capex guide ~$740B vs. ~$150B of identifiable AI revenue (OpenAI ~$50B + Anthropic ~$65B + Microsoft AI ~$37B). Double counting (lab spend is cloud revenue) cuts both ways.
UBS: hyperscaler unsecured bonds YTD, all currencies ($157B USD). Narrower scope than the mid-July $244B figure, so not a decline. UBS sees $270-290B for 2026.
Assumes commitments still ~$1.4T (no 2026 total found) vs. ~$50B run-rate. Nvidia's $100B LOI was replaced by a ~$30B equity stake.
Ornn OCPI H100 SXM $3.13/hr vs $2.59 on Oct 4 (+20% in 11 days); short-window change, not YoY. Direction: rising.
Briefly touched 300bp on Oct 15; S&P Global: trading like BB/B credit. From search snippet.
3.23% per FRED (via search snippet; FRED unreachable from here).
Lowest in the monthly series (since Sep 2008; median 5.27%). Dec 1999 ~2.0% (recalled).
Estimate: CMV's Jun-30 market cap ($78.10T) scaled by the Wilshire 5000 move to Oct 14, over BEA Q2-2026 GDP ($32.56T). ±2pp. Fed Z.1 basis reads ~288-294% (different method; don't splice).
SPY daily holdings, top 10 lines (GOOGL and GOOG counted separately). Top 10 companies: 40.3%. Primary source; earlier chartrow readings may use a different method.
$1,453.8B vs $1,059.7B a year earlier. Record $1,502B in Jun-26; Jul-26 saw the largest monthly drop on record, then a rebound.

triggers.name: Yield curve (10y − 3m)
triggers.detail: Un-inverted to +78 bp after an inversion in the last 18 months (historically the dangerous phase)

triggers.name: Hyperscaler capex guidance cut
triggers.detail: All four raised 2026 guides through Q2 (Big-4 ~$735-750B vs ~$640B in Jan). Microsoft's lower figure is an accounting change, not a cut. Next check: late-Oct Q3 calls.

triggers.name: AI credit repricing
triggers.detail: CoreWeave 5y CDS hit a record ~1,190bp (Oct 15), pricing over 60% odds of default; its 2031 bonds yield ~15%. Oracle CDS touched 300bp (295 on Oct 19), trading like BB/B credit. Goldman: AI high-yield spreads >350bp and data-center debt >400bp vs ~250bp for non-AI BB/B. Amazon, Alphabet and Meta CDS at record wides.

triggers.name: Hyperscaler bond demand
triggers.detail: No jumbo hyperscaler deal since mid-September (earnings blackout ending). Goldman warns AI bond supply could outrun demand; new-issue concessions ~12bp vs ~2bp in 2025. Issuance ~$223B YTD (UBS, Sep 7).

triggers.name: AI revenue quality
triggers.detail: OpenAI run-rate reports revised down ~$20B on definitions; Big-3 net income inflated by mark-to-market gains on AI-lab stakes (Amazon $53B, Alphabet $98B).

triggers.name: GPU oversupply (rents falling)
triggers.detail: H100 rents rising through 2026 - capacity is scarce.

triggers.name: Power / grid bottleneck
triggers.detail: PJM called emergency demand response Oct 13-14 (within ~900MW of its reserve margin); FERC rejected PJM's data-center curtailment plan (Oct 9); a Microsoft-linked UK data center may slip to the 2030s over grid delays.

triggers.name: Fed tightening
triggers.detail: Rate 3.75-4.00% after the Sep 16 hike. Markets price ~15% odds of another hike on Oct 28 but ~89% by December; 10y ~5.1%. Warsh: AI's path 'likely to be a very bumpy one'.

triggers.name: Official-sector warnings
triggers.detail: IMF GFSR (Oct 13) names an AI-driven correction as a near-term trigger; Georgieva (Oct 16): the world economy is 'dangerously reliant' on AI for growth. IMF adverse case: AI investment bust cuts US GDP 1.8% by 2028.

triggers.name: Crowding & sentiment
triggers.detail: BofA Oct FMS: long semiconductors is the most crowded trade; AI bubble is the #2 tail risk; net 37% overweight tech (most since Aug 2020). AAII is 48% bearish - not euphoric.

due.name: US firms using AI in production

history.summary: AI is delivering, and prices and financing are stretched to match. 4 of 16 warning signs are flashing, including AI credit stress, the yield curve and falling chip stocks. The S&P 500 hasn't broken its 200-day trend, which historically is the first sign a correction is starting.

notes: Oct 19: demand and financing are pulling apart. TSMC, ASML, Anthropic's adjusted profit and GPU rents all point to supply-constrained demand, while CoreWeave's CDS prices majority default odds and chip stocks had their longest losing streak since 2008. Next tests: Meta (Oct 21), Microsoft and Alphabet (Oct 28), Amazon (about Oct 29) capex guides, and the FOMC on Oct 28.
Capability instruments are saturating (METR horizon, SWE-bench Verified, ARC-AGI-2, FrontierMath T4 v2). Successors to watch: ARC-AGI-3, SWE-bench Pro, Epoch ECI.
Calendar Q3 2026 hyperscaler earnings (late Oct) and Nvidia Q3 FY27 (late Nov) will refresh most adoption and financing inputs.
BTOS changed its question in Nov 2025; only post-change readings are used.
Forward P/E is ~19.1 (FactSet, Oct 9) against a CAPE of 41.5: today's prices lean heavily on expected earnings growth (Q3 EPS +29.6% YoY expected). An earnings miss matters more than usual.
AI capex is estimated at a third to half of recent US GDP growth (ING, WSJ) - a bust would hit the real economy, not just markets.
